p: What is the reason that we recite … in accordance with

What is the reason that we recite that passage: Blessed be the name of His glorious kingdom for ever and ever, even though it does not appear in the Torah? The Gemara answers: We recite it in accordance with
which Rabbi Shimon ben Lakish interpreted homiletically.

Moses our teacher did not say it … Shall we not recite it? … Jacob said it. … they established that … should be recited surreptitiously.

Moses our teacher did not say it in the Torah as part of Shema. Shall we not recite it? But Jacob said it. In order to resolve this dilemma they established that this passage should be recited surreptitiously.
the school of Rabbi Ami said:
analogous to the daughter of a king who smelled … spices … the pot … If she tells … she will be disgraced,

p: should recite it aloud due to the grievance of the heretics. … In Neharde’a, … where there are no heretics,

should recite it aloud due to the grievance of the heretics. It was instituted to prevent the heretics from claiming that the Jews are surreptitiously reciting inappropriate statements. The Gemara adds: In Neharde’a, where there are no heretics,
they recite it surreptitiously even now.
